parent_request.rule: The parent request must already be persisted and its requester, session, task, workspace identity, and policy version must match the child request.

selection.rule: Selection is non-empty, references only entries in the immediate parent request, and includes every member of each selected dependency_group.

approval.rule: Every apply and retry is revalidated against its own immutable manifest, current policy, workspace identity, file identities, base content, and patch digest.

subset_request.rule: Each selected parent entry receives a deterministic child entry ID scoped to the parent request digest, so per-entry outcomes remain unique and durable.

entry_outcomes.rule: Durable transaction journals and applied_change_entries record each child manifest entry independently.

errors: partial_dependency_group rejects a selection that omits any member of a selected dependency group.
parent_request_missing rejects a child manifest when its referenced parent digest is not durably persisted.
parent_request_context_changed rejects parent/child requester, session, task, workspace identity, or policy mismatches.
subset_entry_changed rejects a child entry whose immutable projection differs from its selected parent entry.
subset_reuses_parent_approval rejects an attempted child request with the parent request digest.
change_set_conflicted requires a fresh preview, subset manifest, digest, and approval after revalidation detects changed policy, workspace identity, file identity, content, or patch.

compatibility.legacy_request: Requests without parent_request_digest and selected_entry_ids decode as root requests only; they cannot be interpreted as subset requests.
compatibility.lineage: A child request carries the immediate parent request digest and selected parent entry IDs in its authorization digest and manifest projection; UI metadata is not an authorization source.
compatibility.approval: Parent approvals are never valid for children because the child authorization envelope has a distinct request digest.
compatibility.retry: A conflict is terminal for that manifest. Recovery starts from a newly prepared request and repeats authorization and identity validation.
compatibility.dependency_groups: A dependency group is indivisible at every selection, persistence, and recovery boundary.
